## Summary (human-written)
<!-- Write this yourself, not with an AI tool. 2-5 sentences: the problem, why
     this approach, and what you checked yourself. -->

## Why
After a multi-turn rollout is repinned to another generator, that generator currently recomputes a prefix absent from its local GPU cache. Add an opt-in vLLM Mooncake Store integration so independent generators can reuse KV from shared CPU DRAM.

For example, generator A produces a turn under policy 5. Generator B can load its prompt and completed decode blocks for the next turn. After B loads policy 6, the same prompt misses policy-5 KV; A can still reuse policy 5. Individual weight updates never clear the shared pool.

## What changed
- Configure `MooncakeStoreConnector` through the existing `VLLMEngine.Config.extra_engine_args["kv_transfer_config"]`, using vLLM's native dict or config object. Validate a run/model namespace, `kv_both`, and decode-cache saving; enable stable block hashing. Deployment settings use upstream `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH`.
- Pass the loaded policy version into the engine, salt shared KV by that version, and reject weight updates while requests are running. Configure the existing router with `hot_swap=False`.
- Keep the engine loop stepping asynchronous cache work after final outputs, including when no new requests arrive.
- Add deployment documentation and CPU/GPU regression coverage. Initial support is TP=DP=EP=1 per generator; scale independent replicas with `num_generators`.

Reference: [verl #6373](https://github.com/verl-project/verl/pull/6373) and [vLLM Store documentation](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage/). Policy-version namespaces avoid a per-replica global Store reset during asynchronous generator updates.

## Testing
- Devgpu, two H100s, one local Master, two independent generator processes, real RDMA and CPU DRAM: **passed**. Cached tokens: cold 0; cross-generator prompt 496; next turn 544 (512-token prompt plus decode KV); changed weights 0; old-policy replica 496.
- `pytest tests/rl/unit_tests/cpu/test_generator.py tests/rl/unit_tests/cpu/test_engine_loop.py -q`: **101 passed, 1 skipped**. Includes native-config passthrough and validation, background progress beyond one engine-step burst, and loaded-version isolation.
- `pre-commit run --all-files`: non-type checks pass after formatting. Pyrefly reports 40 diagnostics, identical to clean base `ff96670a26c7079bc1b9049f5b6942adf35567c1`; no unrelated auto-edits retained.
- Repository `pr-review` skill used; two independent review lenses, fixes applied and correctness re-reviewed with no unresolved findings. The native-config follow-up was self-reviewed and retested on devgpu.

## Numerics / limitations
Cold vs. shared-cache greedy tokens match; sampled logprobs pass the smoke test tolerance. Trainer loss/grad-norm parity and end-to-end RL performance were not measured. The test is on one host; multi-node performance is unverified. Automatic NIC selection encountered retries before succeeding, so this run provides no bandwidth claim.

Tested with torch `2.15.0+cu132`, vLLM distribution `1.0.0.dev20261005+cu132`, and Mooncake `0.3.13.post1`. This host used DMA-BUF (`WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0`) and IPv4 worker addresses. Multi-rank scheduler synchronization, session-based Store eviction, the GPU session holder, batch-invariant/reset-on-load configurations, and standalone `generate.py` support remain outside this draft.

+# Distributed CPU KV cache
+
+Titan RL uses vLLM's
+[`MooncakeStoreConnector`](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/features/mooncake_store_connector_usage/)
+to share prompt and optional decode KV across generators through a distributed
+CPU DRAM pool. Generators keep their local GPU cache; misses recompute from the
+request's full token history.
+
+Store manages CPU capacity and eviction; vLLM manages GPU blocks. The shared pool
+works without prefill/decode disaggregation. The separate
+[`MooncakeConnector`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/mooncake/mooncake_connector.py)
+handles point-to-point prefill/decode transfers.
+
+## Setup
+
+Install a compatible Mooncake SDK on each generator host (tested:
+`mooncake-transfer-engine==0.3.13.post1`). RDMA requires RNICs, GPU memory
+registration, and the SDK's native libraries. Start a reachable Master for metadata:
+
+```bash
+mooncake_master --rpc_port=50051
+```
+
+Set `MOONCAKE_CONFIG_PATH` in every generator process to a local JSON file:
+
+```json
+{
+  "mode": "embedded",
+  "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
+  "master_server_address": "MASTER_HOST:50051",
+  "global_segment_size": "8GB",
+  "local_buffer_size": "1GB",
+  "protocol": "rdma",
+  "device_name": "",
+  "enable_offload": false
+}
+```
+
+- `global_segment_size` is DRAM **per worker**: four workers at 8 GB use 32 GB.
+  Leave room for weight-prefetch buffers and other host processes.
+- `enable_offload` controls the **disk tier**; CPU offload works with `false`.
+
+Host-specific settings used in the RDMA test:
+
+- Set `expandable_segments:False` in both `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF` and
+  `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` before importing PyTorch. Expandable allocations
+  have not been validated.
+- Set `WITH_NVIDIA_PEERMEM=0` for the tested SDK's DMA-BUF path.
+- Set `VLLM_HOST_IP` only if auto-detection fails. Use a routable address for
+  multiple hosts; `127.0.0.1` was used for the single-host test.
+
+## Generator configuration
+
+```python
+from vllm.config import KVTransferConfig
+
+from torchtitan.rl.generator.vllm.engine import VLLMEngine
+from torchtitan.rl.routing.inter_generator import InterGeneratorRouter
+
+engine = VLLMEngine.Config(
+    kv_transfer_config=KVTransferConfig(
+        kv_connector="MooncakeStoreConnector",
+        kv_role="kv_both",
+        kv_connector_extra_config={
+            "cache_prefix": "unique-run-and-model-id",
+            "save_decode_cache": True,
+        },
+    ),
+)
+generator_router = InterGeneratorRouter.Config(hot_swap=False)
+```
+
+- Use a shared, non-empty `cache_prefix` that is **new for each run or restart**,
+  including checkpoint resume. Generators sharing KV must match model, dtype,
+  KV layout, runtime versions, and hash settings, including any `PYTHONHASHSEED`
+  override. Prefix caching and hashing otherwise use vLLM defaults.
+- `kv_both` enables reads and writes; `save_decode_cache=True` also saves generated
+  KV. Other native roles and save options pass through.
+
+## Weight and cache lifecycle
+
+- Load trainer weights before the first request. Titan includes the **loaded
+  policy version** in cache keys so weight updates cannot reuse stale KV.
+- Keep `generator_router.hot_swap=False` to drain model calls before weight
+  updates, and `reset_kv_cache_on_model_state_dict_load=False`: asynchronous saves
+  can still hold GPU blocks after a response. The engine drains pending transfers.
+- Old policy entries remain available until Store evicts them. Do not call
+  `reset_prefix_cache(reset_connector=True)` on a replica; it can clear the
+  shared Store globally.
+
+## Supported configurations
+
+- **Multi-GPU:** Titan's TP and DP/EP layouts are supported. TP ranks coordinate
+  KV lookup and completion using shared logical request IDs while retaining
+  rank-local vLLM IDs; DP groups coordinate progress. Use `num_generators` for
+  independent replicas.
+- **Connector:** direct `MooncakeStoreConnector` only; multi-GPU mode requires
+  vLLM's built-in implementation. `kv_transfer_config=None` disables it.
+- **Sessions:** `session_kv_holder` retains local GPU KV; releasing it does not
+  remove shared Store entries.
+- **Unsupported:** `MultiConnector`, other connectors, batch-invariant mode,
+  and standalone `generate.py`.
+
+## TP coordination
+

+"""Coordinate Mooncake cache decisions between external-launcher TP schedulers.
+
+Schedulers in a TP group agree on request order, cache hits, transfer completion,
+and when to release GPU blocks. Each DP replica has its own requests and TP
+group. Upstream Mooncake workers transfer each rank's KV data.
+
+Each request has one shared Titan ID, but vLLM may assign a different internal
+ID on each rank. Map completion reports to Titan IDs before aggregation, then
+map results back to local vLLM IDs before updating each scheduler.
+
+Cache-hit flow within one TP group (TP=2)::
+
+    TP leader: prefix lookup
+                 |
+                 v
+    Broadcast lookup result and LoadSpec to TP schedulers
+                 |
+                 v
+    Each scheduler allocates local GPU blocks
+                 |
+                 v
+    Each scheduler builds its worker's transfer metadata
+                 |
+         +-------+--------+
+         v                v
+    Worker 0 loads   Worker 1 loads
+    its KV shard     its KV shard
+         |                |
+         +-------+--------+
+                 v
+    All-gather completion reports
+                 |
+                 v
+    Each scheduler aggregates the same reports
+                 |
+                 v
+    Update request state and GPU block references consistently
+
+LoadSpec describes cached token ranges and tail boundaries. Worker metadata
+includes the local GPU block IDs assigned after allocation. Pending lookups
+retry on later steps; completion reports may also arrive in different steps.

+    """A priority heap with a shared logical-ID tie-break instead of local IDs."""

+    def __init__(self, logical_ids: dict[str, str]) -> None:

+        self._heap: list[tuple[int, float, str, Request]] = []

+    def _entry(self, request: Request) -> tuple[int, float, str, Request]:
+        return (
+            request.priority,
+            request.arrival_time,
+            self._logical_ids[request.request_id],
+            request,
+        )

+    def add_request(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        heapq.heappush(self._heap, self._entry(request))

+    def pop_request(self) -> Request:
+        return heapq.heappop(self._heap)[-1]
+
+    def peek_request(self) -> Request:
+        return self._heap[0][-1]
+
+    def prepend_request(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        self.add_request(request)
+
+    def prepend_requests(self, requests: RequestQueue) -> None:
+        for request in requests:
+            self.add_request(request)
+
+    def remove_request(self, request: Request) -> None:
+        self._heap.remove(self._entry(request))
+        heapq.heapify(self._heap)
+
+    def remove_requests(self, requests: Iterable[Request]) -> None:
+        ids = {request.request_id for request in requests}
+        self._heap = [entry for entry in self._heap if entry[-1].request_id not in ids]
+        heapq.heapify(self._heap)
+
+    def __bool__(self) -> bool:
+        return bool(self._heap)
+
+    def __len__(self) -> int:
+        return len(self._heap)
+
+    def __iter__(self) -> Iterator[Request]:
+        return (entry[-1] for entry in sorted(self._heap))
